Simulated promotions: a continuous endogenous treatment

Source: R/data.R
promotion.Rd

Employees choose hours of training partly on an unobserved ability that also drives promotion, so training is endogenous. A randomly assigned training subsidy shifts training; in this simulation it has no direct effect on promotion, so the true exclusion-restriction violation is zero. Training pays off more under a supportive manager. The same file is shipped as inst/extdata/promotion.dta for the Stata command.

Usage

promotion

Format

A data frame with 4,000 rows and 6 variables:

promoted

Promoted (0/1); the outcome.

training

Hours of training (standardized); the endogenous treatment.

subsidy

Training subsidy (standardized); the instrument.

tenure

Tenure (standardized); a control.

manager

Supportive manager (0/1); a control and moderator.

team

Team identifier, 200 teams of 20; for clustered standard errors.

Source

Simulated.

Details

Data-generating process (data-raw/example_data.do, seed 20260613): training = 0.7 subsidy + 0.3 tenure + 0.2 manager + a, promoted = 1[-0.3 + 0.5 training + 0.4 tenure + 0.3 manager + 0.4 training x manager + e > 0], with a ~ N(0, 1) the unobserved ability and e = 0.5 a + sqrt(0.75) u, u ~ N(0, 1).

Examples

data(promotion)
summary(promotion)
#>     promoted         training           subsidy              tenure
